# XY Forever serial protocol 1.13

XY Forever is a boot menu and firmware manager for the teenage engineering OP-XY. While its menu runs, the OP-XY's processor B answers this protocol over USB. Tools use it to list, read, write and delete files, take screenshots, stage and install builds, set the default firmware and restart the device.

Transport: USB CDC serial, the raw frame stream (table below). The device answers only while the XY Forever menu runs: after an XY Forever restart, or when the OP-XY is powered on with PLAY held (release it at the logo).

All numbers are little-endian. Byte counts are in decimal unless written in hex (`0x...`).

The machine-readable specification is [`protocol/v1.json`](../protocol/v1.json); this page, the firmware header, the host module and the TypeScript module (`clients/ts/src/v1.ts`) are generated from it. Version 1.13 describes the device as it is today. "Since" names the version that introduced an entry's current form.

## Transport

How a tool reaches the protocol. `verified` is true for facts read from device sessions or the code, false for facts nobody has checked yet.

| Fact | Value | Verified | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| usb vendor id | `0x2367` | yes | teenage engineering: the stock serial identity (`scripts/usb_timeline.py`), which the product build (188 and later) falls back to when a boot-time check fails, and which builds before 188 always used |
| usb product id | `0x0021` | yes | the stock OS uses the same id with no serial interface (MTP, vendor class 0xFF; another mode is 0x8021, class 0x01), so a filter on both ids finds only XY Forever's service on the stock identity; a tool must accept this pair and `product_usb_ids` |
| product usb ids | `2367:0021` | yes | since product build 189-002 the composite (this CDC serial interface, MTP on interface 2) has the stock pair 2367:0021 (`xyf_build.py` MTP_USB_IDS), told apart from the stock OS's MTP and the stock serial fallback by its device class 0xEF (IAD); builds 188 to 189-001 used pid.codes' test pair 1209:0001; not yet seen on the device |
| usb product | `OP_XY Boot` | yes | the product string as macOS reports it in the session logs (two log lines show `OP-XY Boot`); informational: filter on the ids |
| interface classes | `0x02, 0x0a` | yes | USB CDC: communications (0x02) and data (0x0A); on macOS the port is `/dev/cu.usbmodem*` |
| stream | `frames` | yes | the CDC data interface carries exactly the frame stream described here, in both directions, with no other framing; the simulator's TCP port carries the same bytes |
| line settings | `ignored` | yes | baud rate, parity, stop bits and flow control do not matter (an API that needs a baud rate may pass any); open the port raw (no echo, no line editing) |
| control lines | `unknown` | no | whether the device needs DTR or RTS set: `xyf_host.py` leaves them as macOS sets them on open |
| usb serial number | `unknown` | no | macOS names the port `cu.usbmodem<string>1`, which suggests a serial-number string; a browser may need one to find the port again after a restart without asking the user |
| simulator port | `7341` | yes | default TCP port of the device simulator (`python3 -m xy_forever.sim`, 127.0.0.1 only; control on the next port), one client at a time |

## Frames

Every message, in both directions, is one frame:

| Offset | Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `magic` | bytes[2] | ASCII `XF` (0x58 0x46) |
| 2 | `type` | u8 | message type: a request (< 0x80), its reply (request type + 0x80) or an event |
| 3 | `seq` | u8 | chosen by the tool for each request; the reply carries the same value; events use 0 |
| 4 | `length` | u32 | payload bytes, at most `max_payload` |
| 8 | `payload` | rest | `length` bytes |
| 8 + length | `crc` | u32 | CRC-32 of magic, type, seq, length and payload |

The CRC is the zlib CRC-32 (polynomial 0xEDB88320, initial value and final XOR 0xFFFFFFFF, as Python's zlib.crc32) over every byte before it.
Example, `hello` with seq 1: `58 46 01 01 00 00 00 00 4c 8d 06 32`.

Payload fields are packed without gaps. Types: `u8`, `u16`, `u32` unsigned little-endian; `bytes[N]` exactly N bytes; `cstr` text ending in one NUL; `text` text to the end of the payload, no NUL; `rest` raw bytes to the end of the payload. Each text field names its encoding (ASCII or UTF-8; see the rules). Optional fields come last and are all present or all absent. A reply payload is a `u32` status followed by the fields listed for it.

## Rules

- Request types are below 0x80. A reply has the request's type plus 0x80 and the request's seq, and its payload starts with a u32 status code (0 = ok); the fields listed under each command follow it.
- One request at a time: send a request, then wait for its reply (or the command's timeout) before sending the next. The device handles requests one by one and its receive buffer is small.
- Send `hello` first. Until the device has answered a `hello` since it started, it answers every other request with status `state` and does nothing.
- A request type this build does not answer gets status `unsupported`. The `cmds` key of the `hello` reply lists the types a build answers; tools send no others and tell the user to update XY Forever instead. A command with an optional build switch is missing from a build without it; a command whose switch is not optional is in every build that has this service (the firmware does not build without it).
- Devices that send `proto=1` and no `cmds` (XY Forever builds 153 and earlier) speak 1.0 without the `hello` keys added in 1.1: tools treat every 1.0 command as answered (one the build lacks gets status 2) and expect no status above 13.
- Tools drop frames whose seq or type does not match the request they wait for, and reset their frame parser after a timeout: a late reply to an earlier request is then ignored.
- After a `link` error, later file commands return `link` at once until the device's 60 s lost limit, a restart, or (from build 159) the device's own recovery.
- Events are frames the device sends on its own, with seq 0 and a type of 0x80 or above that is not a reply to the request outstanding. Today there is one, `log` (0xD0). Tools accept events at any time, also while waiting for a reply, and ignore types they do not know.
- Both sides decode byte by byte. On a wrong magic, a length above `max_payload` or a CRC mismatch the decoder drops one byte and searches again, so a frame after noise or a damaged frame is still found (the `streams` in the spec file are test cases). A frame cut short (a write that stopped part way, bytes lost on the way) is dropped once no byte has arrived for `idle_reset_ms`, so a request sent after that silence is found. Tools send each frame in one go (no pause of `idle_reset_ms` inside a frame). Builds 181 and earlier never time out a partial frame: it waits until as many bytes as its header announced have arrived, swallowing the start of the next requests; a tool clears that by sending `put_chunk` bytes of 0x00 and then `hello`, up to 5 times, until the `hello` is answered (5 rounds cover the largest frame).
- Requests are decoded strictly: exactly the listed fields (the device checks lengths). Replies and events are decoded leniently: a tool ignores bytes after the fields it knows, so a later 1.x can add fields at the end. A reply or event marked `extensible: false` ends in `rest` or `text` and can never gain fields; a later version that needs more adds a command. An error reply holds the fields its `on_error` names, or the status alone. A common status sent as such (`state` before `hello`, `unsupported`, `busy`) always comes alone; a command that lists the same status among its own errors may send its `on_error` fields with it (`file.write_staged` and `boot.install` do for `state`), so decoders accept both.
- Optional fields come last and are all present or all absent (`optional_fields: all_or_none` on the layout): a `file.read` request is the path alone, or the path, offset and length.
- Each `cstr` and `text` field states its encoding. `ascii`: bytes 0x01 to 0x7F. `utf-8`: file and folder names, which MTP clients and computers make with any characters. Limits: `max_bytes` counts bytes, not characters; a name never holds NUL, and `/` separates its parts; the device compares names as bytes, without Unicode normalisation (macOS may send decomposed accents, Windows composed ones, so one visible name can be two files). The device checks the `/yaffs2/` start, the parts (no empty, `.` or `..`), the NUL and control bytes (below 0x20, and 0x7F: `refused` since build 155), and passes every other byte to the stock file system unchanged: invalid UTF-8 is not refused.
- The device checks request lengths exactly (except where a command says the payload is ignored); a request with the wrong length is refused with the status the command lists.
- Version 1 never renumbers a type or status, changes a meaning or changes a request layout. A later 1.x may add commands, status codes, events, `hello` keys and fields at the end of a reply: tools ignore reply bytes after the fields they know and `hello` keys they do not know, and show an unknown status by number as a failure. A tool stops when the major version in `proto` is not the one it speaks. Developer commands are outside this promise.
- Commands marked destructive change what the OP-XY stores. Each binds its request to what it changes: the data it writes (a SHA-256 the tool sends again as confirmation; `library.set_default`: the id), or, for `file.delete`, `file.rmdir` and `file.mkdir`, the SHA-256 of the path bytes (without the NUL; `file.rename` and `file.copy`: both paths and the NUL between them). Tools must show the user what will be written or removed and ask before sending one.

## Constants

| Name | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `header_bytes` | 8 | magic, type, seq and length |
| `trailer_bytes` | 4 | the CRC-32 |
| `max_payload` | 4160 | largest payload in either direction; a frame announcing more is treated as noise |
| `max_data` | 4096 | largest file or image data in one reply |
| `max_read` | 1024 | largest `length` of a ranged `file.read`, and the most data `screen.read` returns per reply |
| `put_chunk` | 1024 | data bytes per `stage.data` request that tools should send: the device's USB receive buffer holds 2048 bytes, and a 4 KiB frame overflowed it (no reply) |
| `max_path` | 240 | largest device path, including its NUL |
| `max_stage` | 7340032 | largest staged image (7 MiB) |
| `max_log_text` | 200 | largest text of a `log` event |
| `idle_reset_ms` | 250 | the device drops a partial frame once its receive buffer has been empty for this long (XY Forever builds 181 and earlier never did) |
| `max_hello` | 200 | largest `hello` text; a build's text is fixed but for its stage-2 parts (170 bytes in the product build without stage 2), checked when it is compiled |

## Status codes

Every reply starts with one. A tool shows a code it does not know by number and treats it as a failure. Besides the errors listed under each command, these can come to any command, as the status alone (whatever its `on_error` says): `state`, to any command but `hello`: the device has not answered a `hello` since it started; nothing was done. `unsupported`, to any command but `hello`: this build does not answer the type (it is not in `cmds`). `busy`, to any command but `hello`: a job is running, or its write window is still closing after `job.status` said it ended: every command that needs processor A, the staging or a boot waits for it (`diag.status`, `screen.read`, `service.hold`, `job.status` and `job.cancel` are answered).

| Code | Name | Since | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | `ok` | 1.0 | done |
| 1 | `bad_request` | 1.0 | malformed request: wrong length, a value out of its allowed set, an invalid path or id |
| 2 | `unsupported` | 1.0 | this build does not answer this type (named `unknown` before 1.1) |
| 3 | `state` | 1.0 | wrong order: no `hello` yet, nothing staged, staging incomplete; the same request will not succeed until something else changes |
| 4 | `range` | 1.0 | an offset or address outside what the command allows |
| 5 | `crc` | 1.0 | a CRC-32 differs (staged data, or a written file read back) |
| 6 | `sha` | 1.0 | a SHA-256 differs (staged data or the confirmation token) |
| 7 | `storage` | 1.0 | a file-system call on the device failed |
| 8 | `not_found` | 1.0 | no such file |
| 9 | `too_large` | 1.0 | a size above its limit (staging capacity, boot partition, whole-file read) |
| 10 | `image` | 1.0 | the staged image is not acceptable for this install |
| 11 | `install` | 1.0 | the boot-partition write or its read-back check failed |
| 12 | `link` | 1.0 | processor A did not answer a request processor B passed on to it |
| 13 | `identity` | 1.0 | stock code in the device's memory differs from the checked bootloader image; the command did not run |
| 14 | `refused` | 1.1 | well formed, but forbidden by the device's safety policy (a path the file engine refuses, or, for a change, outside the write area: since 1.13 all of `/yaffs2/` except `/yaffs2/bootloader.dev` and `/yaffs2/upgrade` with all below it) |
| 15 | `busy` | 1.10 | a job (`mods.apply`) is running, or B is still closing A's write window after it ended (seconds); retry later, or `job.cancel` a running job |
| 16 | `cancelled` | 1.1 | the job was cancelled (not sent by any command yet) |
| 17 | `no_content` | 1.10 | the library entry's content is not installed in `/yaffs2/content/` (a mod set built on the device, or any entry while another one's content is installed): it is listed but does not boot as it is; make it the default to install its content |
| 18 | `started` | 1.10 | the request started a job (`library.set_default`: the content switch); follow it with `job.status`, whose end is the request's result |
| 19 | `declined` | 1.11 | the user refused the command at the device's Confirm on device prompt, or nobody answered it in time; nothing was done (not sent by any command yet: the prompt is not built) |

## Commands

| Type | Name | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 0x01 | [`hello`](#0x01-hello) | greet the device; required before any other command |
| 0x03 | [`file.read`](#0x03-fileread) | read a file, whole (at most 4096 bytes) or a range |
| 0x04 | [`screen.read`](#0x04-screenread) | read part of the display framebuffer (screenshot) |
| 0x10 | [`stage.begin`](#0x10-stagebegin) | announce an image to stage in RAM |
| 0x11 | [`stage.data`](#0x11-stagedata) | send the next piece of the staged image |
| 0x12 | [`stage.end`](#0x12-stageend) | check the staged image against its CRC-32 and SHA-256 |
| 0x13 | [`file.write_staged`](#0x13-filewrite_staged) | write the staged image to a file under /yaffs2/ (the write area) |
| 0x14 | [`file.list`](#0x14-filelist) | list one folder, a page at a time |
| 0x15 | [`file.delete`](#0x15-filedelete) | delete one file |
| 0x16 | [`file.rmdir`](#0x16-filermdir) | remove one empty folder |
| 0x17 | [`file.mkdir`](#0x17-filemkdir) | create one folder |
| 0x18 | [`file.rename`](#0x18-filerename) | rename or move one file or folder |
| 0x19 | [`file.copy`](#0x19-filecopy) | copy one file on the device |
| 0x20 | [`boot.install`](#0x20-bootinstall) | install the staged XY Forever build into the boot partition |
| 0x21 | [`boot.uninstall`](#0x21-bootuninstall) | put the stock 1.2.1 os.ldr back into the boot partition |
| 0x30 | [`device.reboot`](#0x30-devicereboot) | restart both processors |
| 0x31 | [`menu.continue`](#0x31-menucontinue) | leave the menu and boot the default firmware |
| 0x32 | [`service.hold`](#0x32-servicehold) | keep the device in the menu across restarts |
| 0x40 | [`library.set_default`](#0x40-libraryset_default) | make a library entry the default firmware |
| 0x41 | [`tfw.check`](#0x41-tfwcheck) | check that a firmware package on the device is official and that the device's own keys open it |
| 0x43 | [`library.boot`](#0x43-libraryboot) | boot a library entry once, as PLAY on it in the library menu |
| 0x44 | [`mods.apply`](#0x44-modsapply) | start assembling mod firmware on the device (a job) |
| 0x45 | [`job.status`](#0x45-jobstatus) | progress of the running or last job |
| 0x46 | [`job.cancel`](#0x46-jobcancel) | stop the running job |

A typical session: `hello`; then reads (`file.read`, `screen.read`); to write, `stage.begin`, `stage.data` in order, `stage.end`, then one of `file.write_staged`, `boot.install`, `boot.uninstall`.

### 0x01 `hello`

Greet the device; required before any other command. Answers in every state. While searching for the device, a tool may send `hello` every 0.5 s on the open port until a reply with status ok arrives. The reply tells the tool what the device supports: the protocol version, the build, the limits and the commands it answers. 1.1 added the keys from `build` on; a device without `cmds` is a pre-v1 device (see the rules).

Request: empty (the device ignores any payload).

| Reply field, after the status (1 to 200 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `info` | text ASCII, 1..200 B | ASCII, `XYF1` and then `key=value` items, separated by `;`; no NUL; at most `max_hello` bytes. The keys are listed below; tools ignore keys they do not know. |

On an error: the status only. Errors: none of its own. The reply never gains fields (it ends in `text`). Tool timeout: 5 s. Since 1.1.

#### `hello` keys

The `hello` text: `XYF1`, then these keys in this order, each as `;key=value`. A build's text never changes while it runs, except `stage2` and the stage-2 command's bit of `cmds`: both are set before the reply to the first `hello` of a boot when stage 2 loads, and cleared again if stage 2 stops answering as it should. Tools ignore keys they do not know and must not rely on the order.

| Key | Since | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `service` | 1.0 | `usb`: the service that answers |
| `role` | 1.0 | `b`: the processor that answers |
| `proto` | 1.0 | `1.13`: protocol version `MAJOR.MINOR` (pre-v1 devices: `1`) |
| `install` | 1.0 | `stock-88a06a7e`: the boot-partition writer `boot.install` uses (the stock bootloader's own, at 0x88a06a7e) |
| `build` | 1.1 | XY Forever build number, decimal |
| `mode` | 1.1 | build mode (`product`, the only mode with this service) |
| `payload` | 1.1 | `4160`: `max_payload` |
| `read` | 1.1 | `1024`: `max_read` |
| `stage` | 1.1 | `7340032`: `max_stage` |
| `cmds` | 1.1 | the request types this build answers: 32 lowercase hex digits, a 128-bit number written most significant digit first, in which bit t (value 2^t) is set when type t is answered (Python: `int(cmds, 16) >> t & 1`). Derived from each command's build switch when the build is compiled; the stage-2 command's bit is set at run time while stage 2 is loaded |
| `dev` | 1.1 | `1` when the build answers developer commands; absent otherwise |
| `stage2` | 1.6 | the loaded stage 2's version, decimal; `0` when none is loaded (no file, or it failed a check). Always the last key |

The product build answers (170 bytes):

`XYF1;service=usb;role=b;proto=1.13;install=stock-88a06a7e;build=172;mode=product;payload=4160;read=1024;stage=7340032;cmds=000000010000007b001f000303ff00be;dev=1;stage2=0`

### 0x03 `file.read`

Read a file, whole (at most 4096 bytes) or a range. Two forms: with `offset` and `length` (ranged), or the path alone (whole file, `too_large` above 4096 bytes). Use the ranged form: whole-file replies above 1 KiB hung the device in tests. To read any file, read ranges of `max_read` bytes from offset 0 until a reply holds fewer. An offset at or past the end of the file is ok with no data; `range` means the device's seek to the offset failed. A malformed path is `bad_request`; a well-formed one that the device's file policy refuses (a control byte) is `refused` (since build 155; earlier builds passed it to the file system).

| Request field (10 to 248 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | cstr UTF-8, 10..240 B | absolute path under `/yaffs2/`, NUL-terminated; no empty, `.` or `..` parts; no control bytes |
| `offset` | u32 | Optional. First byte to read |
| `length` | u32 | Optional. Bytes to read, at most `max_read` (1..1024) |

| Reply field, after the status (0 to 4096 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `data` | rest, 0..4096 B | ranged form: up to `length` bytes, fewer only at the end of the file; whole form: the whole file |

On an error: the status only. Errors: `bad_request`, `refused`, `link`, `storage`, `not_found`, `range`, `too_large`. The reply never gains fields (it ends in `rest`). Tool timeout: 15 s. Since 1.0.

### 0x04 `screen.read`

Read part of the display framebuffer (screenshot). Reads memory only. The framebuffer is 245760 (0x3C000) bytes: 480 columns, stored right to left, of 256 RGB565 pixels each, top to bottom; the visible picture is the first 216 pixels of each column. A screenshot reads offsets 0, 1024, 2048, ... until it has 245760 bytes. A request that is not exactly 4 bytes, an offset past the end or no valid framebuffer gives `range`.

| Request field (4 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `offset` | u32 | byte offset into the framebuffer (0..245759) |

| Reply field, after the status (5 to 1028 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `framebuffer` | u32 | the framebuffer's address (informational; also sent with `range`) |
| `pixels` | rest, 1..1024 B | up to `max_read` bytes from `offset` |

On an error: the status and `framebuffer`. Errors: `range`. The reply never gains fields (it ends in `rest`). Tool timeout: 5 s. Since 1.0.

### 0x10 `stage.begin`

Announce an image to stage in RAM. Starts a new staging and forgets any earlier one, also when it is refused (a `stage.data` after a refused `stage.begin` is `state`). Staging holds one image in processor B's RAM for `file.write_staged`, `boot.install` or `boot.uninstall`; it does not survive a restart. A size of 0 is also `too_large`.

| Request field (40 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `size` | u32 | image bytes, at most `max_stage` (1..7340032) |
| `crc32` | u32 | CRC-32 of the whole image |
| `sha256` | bytes[32] | SHA-256 of the whole image |

Reply: the status only.

Errors: `bad_request`, `too_large`. Tool timeout: 5 s. Since 1.0.

### 0x11 `stage.data`

Send the next piece of the staged image. In order, without gaps: `range` when `offset` is not the bytes received so far or the data would pass the announced size; a resend of bytes already received, unchanged (a retry after a lost reply), is ok and `received` stays. `state` without a `stage.begin`, and also for a request without data.

| Request field (5 to 4160 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `offset` | u32 | must equal the bytes received so far |
| `data` | rest, 1..4156 B | the next bytes; send `put_chunk` (1024) at a time |

| Reply field, after the status (4 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `received` | u32 | bytes received so far |

On an error: the status only. Errors: `state`, `range`. Tool timeout: 5 s. Since 1.0.

### 0x12 `stage.end`

Check the staged image against its CRC-32 and SHA-256. `state` when not every announced byte arrived. After any error the staging is discarded; start again with `stage.begin`. A repeated `stage.end` after an ok one (a retry after a lost reply) is ok again and keeps the staging, until `boot.install`, `boot.uninstall` or `file.copy` uses it up or a `stage.begin` replaces it.

Request: empty (the device ignores any payload).

Reply: the status only.

Errors: `state`, `crc`, `sha`. Tool timeout: 10 s. Since 1.0.

### 0x13 `file.write_staged`

Write the staged image to a file under /yaffs2/ (the write area). Creates or replaces the file, reads it back and compares its CRC-32 (`crc` on a difference). A path the device's write check rejects is `refused` (1.0: `bad_request`): since 1.13 the write area is all of `/yaffs2/` except the dev-menu marker `/yaffs2/bootloader.dev` and the stock updater's inbox `/yaffs2/upgrade` (and anything inside it), both any ASCII case and also when reached through a link; also a path with an empty, `.` or `..` part, or, since build 155, a control byte. Before 1.13 the area was `/yaffs2/xy-forever/` and (1.7) `/yaffs2/content/`, no name holding `bootloader`; a request whose length does not match its path is `bad_request`. Needs a complete staging (`state` otherwise). The host tool restarts the device (`device.reboot`) and stages again before each write, the tested path; a second write in the same boot is untested. The host waits 60 s plus 1 s per 20000 bytes. To be replaced by streaming file commands (plan item 2.4).

| Request field (42 to 272 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | cstr UTF-8, 10..240 B | `/yaffs2/` and at least one more character, NUL-terminated; no empty, `.` or `..` parts; no control bytes; never `/yaffs2/bootloader.dev`, never inside `/yaffs2/upgrade/` (1.13); missing folders are created |
| `sha256` | bytes[32] | confirmation: the staged image's SHA-256 again |

| Reply field, after the status (8 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `written` | u32 | bytes written |
| `readback_crc` | u32 | CRC-32 of the file read back |

On an error: every field (zero where not reached). Errors: `bad_request`, `refused`, `state`, `sha`, `link`, `storage`, `not_found`, `crc`. Tool timeout: 60 s. **Destructive**: ask the user first. Build switch `XYF_USB_FILE_WRITE`, not optional: the firmware does not build without it. Since 1.1.

### 0x14 `file.list`

List one folder, a page at a time. One page of a folder's entries in the file system's order, without `.` and `..`; at most 1016 bytes of entries (a reply never passes `max_read`) and 64 entries per page. Each page opens the folder, passes over `skip` entries and closes it again, so a folder that changes between pages may show an entry twice or not at all; a page with `more` 1 may hold no entries. A path the device's file policy refuses (outside `/yaffs2`, an empty, `.` or `..` part, a control byte) is `refused`; a request whose length does not match its path is `bad_request`; a folder that does not exist (or a file) is `not_found`. Reads only: the write window stays as it is.

| Request field (12 to 244 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | cstr UTF-8, 8..240 B | absolute folder path, `/yaffs2` or below, NUL-terminated; a trailing `/` is allowed |
| `skip` | u32 | entries to pass over first: 0, then the previous `skip` plus `count` while `more` is 1 |

| Reply field, after the status (8 to 1024 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `count` | u32 | entries in this page |
| `more` | u32 | 0 = the folder ends in this page; 1 = ask again with skip + count. Whether the listing goes on |
| `entries` | rest, 0..1016 B | `count` entries, each `{u8 kind (0 file, 1 folder, 2 other), u32 size (bytes; 0 for a folder), u8 name_bytes, name}`: the name as UTF-8 bytes, 1 to 255 of them, without the folder or a NUL |

On an error: the status only. Errors: `bad_request`, `refused`, `link`, `storage`, `not_found`. The reply never gains fields (it ends in `rest`). Tool timeout: 30 s. Build switch `XYF_USB_FILE_WRITE`, not optional: the firmware does not build without it. Since 1.5.

### 0x15 `file.delete`

Delete one file. Removes the file through the device's write window (opened by the first change, closed by the device 8 s after the last one, as `file.write_staged`). Never `/yaffs2` itself, `/yaffs2/bootloader.dev` or `/yaffs2/upgrade` and anything inside it (any ASCII case, any spelling, also through a link; 1.13): `refused`, as every path the file policy refuses and every path outside `file.write_staged`'s write area; a wrong confirmation is `sha`. A missing file is `not_found`; a folder (error 21) or any other failure `storage`.

| Request field (42 to 272 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | cstr UTF-8, 10..240 B | absolute path of a file in the write area (`file.write_staged`; 1.13: all of `/yaffs2/` but the marker and `upgrade/`), NUL-terminated |
| `sha256` | bytes[32] | confirmation: the SHA-256 of the path bytes, without the NUL |

| Reply field, after the status (4 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `error` | u32 | the device file system's error number (0 when none; 2 no such object, 21 a folder, 93 a folder not empty) |

On an error: every field (zero where not reached). Errors: `bad_request`, `refused`, `sha`, `link`, `storage`, `not_found`. Tool timeout: 60 s. **Destructive**: ask the user first. Build switch `XYF_USB_FILE_WRITE`, not optional: the firmware does not build without it. Since 1.5.

### 0x16 `file.rmdir`

Remove one empty folder. As `file.delete`, for an empty folder only: a folder that still holds entries is `state` (error 93; remove them first); a file (error 20) or any other failure is `storage`.

| Request field (42 to 272 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | cstr UTF-8, 10..240 B | absolute path of a folder in the write area (as `file.delete`), NUL-terminated |
| `sha256` | bytes[32] | confirmation: the SHA-256 of the path bytes, without the NUL |

| Reply field, after the status (4 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `error` | u32 | the device file system's error number (0 when none; 2 no such object, 20 not a folder, 93 not empty) |

On an error: every field (zero where not reached). Errors: `bad_request`, `refused`, `sha`, `state`, `link`, `storage`, `not_found`. Tool timeout: 60 s. **Destructive**: ask the user first. Build switch `XYF_USB_FILE_WRITE`, not optional: the firmware does not build without it. Since 1.5.

### 0x17 `file.mkdir`

Create one folder. Creates one folder through the write window (as `file.delete`). A missing parent is `not_found`; a name that exists already (error 17) or any other failure is `storage`. Paths the file policy refuses are `refused`.

| Request field (42 to 272 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | cstr UTF-8, 10..240 B | absolute path of the new folder in the write area (as `file.delete`), NUL-terminated; its parent must exist |
| `sha256` | bytes[32] | confirmation: the SHA-256 of the path bytes, without the NUL |

| Reply field, after the status (4 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `error` | u32 | the device file system's error number (0 when none; 2 the parent is missing, 17 the name exists) |

On an error: every field (zero where not reached). Errors: `bad_request`, `refused`, `sha`, `link`, `storage`, `not_found`. Tool timeout: 60 s. **Destructive**: ask the user first. Build switch `XYF_USB_FILE_WRITE`, not optional: the firmware does not build without it. Since 1.5.

### 0x18 `file.rename`

Rename or move one file or folder. Renames, or moves between folders, a file or a whole folder through the write window (as `file.delete`). Both paths must pass `file.delete`'s checks (`refused`); a target that exists is `state` (nothing replaced); a missing source or target parent `not_found`; a folder into itself (error 22) or any other failure `storage`.

| Request field (60 to 512 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | cstr UTF-8, 10..240 B | absolute path of a file or folder in the write area (as `file.delete`), NUL-terminated |
| `target` | cstr UTF-8, 18..240 B | its new path, in the write area (never the marker, never in `upgrade/`); must not exist; its parent must |
| `sha256` | bytes[32] | confirmation: the SHA-256 of the source bytes, a NUL and the target bytes |

| Reply field, after the status (4 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `error` | u32 | the device file system's error number (0 when none; 2 no source or no target parent, 17 the target exists, 22 a folder into itself) |

On an error: every field (zero where not reached). Errors: `bad_request`, `refused`, `sha`, `state`, `link`, `storage`, `not_found`. Tool timeout: 60 s. **Destructive**: ask the user first. Build switch `XYF_USB_FILE_WRITE`, not optional: the firmware does not build without it. Since 1.8.

### 0x19 `file.copy`

Copy one file on the device. Processor B reads the source whole into its staging buffer (at most `stage` bytes, else `too_large`) and writes it to the target as `file.write_staged` does, read back and compared (`crc`); the bytes never cross USB. A staging held before is discarded (`file.write_staged` and `boot.install` then answer `state`). A source `file.read` refuses, or a target `file.write_staged` refuses, is `refused`; a missing source or target folder `not_found`; a target that exists `state` (nothing replaced). After a failed write the device deletes the target. The host waits 60 s plus 1 s per 10000 bytes.

| Request field (60 to 512 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `source` | cstr UTF-8, 10..240 B | absolute path of a file `file.read` may read, NUL-terminated |
| `target` | cstr UTF-8, 18..240 B | the new file's path, as for `file.write_staged`; must not exist; its folder must |
| `sha256` | bytes[32] | confirmation: the SHA-256 of the source bytes, a NUL and the target bytes |

| Reply field, after the status (12 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `bytes` | u32 | bytes read from the source |
| `error` | u32 | the device file system's error number (0 when none; 2 no target folder, 17 the target exists) |
| `partial` | u32 | 0 = no partial target left; 1 = a partial target may remain. After a failed write: whether its target may remain (the device deletes it when it can) |

On an error: every field (zero where not reached). Errors: `bad_request`, `refused`, `sha`, `state`, `link`, `storage`, `not_found`, `too_large`, `crc`. Tool timeout: 60 s. **Destructive**: ask the user first. Build switch `XYF_USB_FILE_WRITE`, not optional: the firmware does not build without it. Since 1.9.

### 0x20 `boot.install`

Install the staged XY Forever build into the boot partition. Accepts only a staged XY Forever build (its cold descriptor and a valid LDR structure; `image` otherwise) that fits the boot partition (`too_large`). Writes with the stock bootloader's own A/B boot-partition writer, then reads the partition back and compares every byte (`install` on any difference). Sends `log` events while it runs. A wrong-length request or no complete staging is `state`. Once the writer has run (`ok` or `install`) the staging is used up; a request refused before writing leaves it as it was. Takes minutes; the host waits up to 900 s.

| Request field (32 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `sha256` | bytes[32] | confirmation: the staged image's SHA-256 again |

| Reply field, after the status (12 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `written` | u32 | non-zero when the boot-partition writer finished |
| `partition` | u32 | active boot partition read back (1 or 2; 0 = none) |
| `sectors` | u32 | 512-byte sectors read back and compared |

On an error: every field (zero where not reached). Errors: `state`, `sha`, `image`, `link`, `too_large`, `install`. Tool timeout: 900 s. **Destructive**: ask the user first. Since 1.0.

### 0x21 `boot.uninstall`

Put the stock 1.2.1 os.ldr back into the boot partition. As `boot.install`, but accepts only the exact stock OP-XY 1.2.1 `os.ldr` (2373336 bytes, SHA-256 `60358afdaa9b58ed40411602f6d5d4e1e3e02553ff2da7e25038e71dd002b52f`). Afterwards the OP-XY boots stock 1.2.1 and this service is gone; files under `/yaffs2/xy-forever/` stay.

| Request field (32 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `sha256` | bytes[32] | confirmation: the staged image's SHA-256 again |

| Reply field, after the status (12 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `written` | u32 | non-zero when the boot-partition writer finished |
| `partition` | u32 | active boot partition read back (1 or 2; 0 = none) |
| `sectors` | u32 | 512-byte sectors read back and compared |

On an error: every field (zero where not reached). Errors: `state`, `sha`, `image`, `link`, `too_large`, `install`. Tool timeout: 900 s. **Destructive**: ask the user first. Since 1.0.

### 0x30 `device.reboot`

Restart both processors. The reply comes first; the device restarts about 50 ms later and the USB port goes away. Wait for the port to come back, then send `hello`. Targets 0 and 2 behave the same today. A target above 2 is `bad_request`; a payload that is neither empty nor 4 bytes counts as no target.

| Request field (0 to 4 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `target` | u32 | Optional. 0 = the XY Forever menu with USB; 1 = the default firmware (OS); 2 = the XY Forever menu with USB. Where the device goes; without it: 2 |

Reply: the status only.

Errors: `bad_request`. Tool timeout: 5 s. Since 1.0.

### 0x31 `menu.continue`

Leave the menu and boot the default firmware. After the ok reply the menu closes and USB goes away. Any other payload, or a mode above 1, is answered with `link` (not `bad_request`); so is a dry run processor A did not accept. Modes 2 and 3 ("open the menu with USB", Test 058, before boot model v3) are not part of v1: the menu is the home loop that answers this protocol, so a tool that is connected is already in the menu.

| Request field (0 to 4 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | u32 | Optional. 0 = boot the default firmware; 1 = dry run: the whole boot path without starting the OS, then back to the menu. Without it: 0 |

Reply: the status only.

Errors: `link`. Tool timeout: 5 s. Since 1.0.

### 0x32 `service.hold`

Keep the device in the menu across restarts.

| Request field (4 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `on` | u32 | 0 = off; 1 = on. On: stay in the XY Forever menu (with USB) across `device.reboot` until power-off |

Reply: the status only.

Errors: `bad_request`. Tool timeout: 5 s. Since 1.0.

### 0x40 `library.set_default`

Make a library entry the default firmware. An entry whose content is not installed (listed as content not installed) first gets its content: B starts the content switch as a job and answers `started` (`job.status`: phase `inputs`, `content` with done/total in files, `finish` while it writes the record and the default; `done` with detail = the id once the default is written; `failed` leaves the default unchanged, `error` 15 with code 1 when `/yaffs2/content/` is not the official set, 2 when the entry would replace an official file; a cut or failure leaves the content state switching, which nothing boots from until this request runs again). A build without the switch answers `no_content` (nothing sent to A). Processor A finds the one entry whose id has this hash and an `os.ldr`, and writes the next of the two state files (`/yaffs2/xy-forever/state-a.txt`, `state-b.txt`). ok means A finished and the menu shows the new default; `storage` means the menu's default did not change. Tools can confirm by reading both state files: the valid one with the higher `seq=` holds `default=ID`.

| Request field (2 to 32 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | cstr ASCII, 2..32 B | library entry id: 1-31 of `a-z 0-9 _ -`, NUL-terminated (the folder name under `/yaffs2/xy-forever/firmware/`) |

| Reply field, after the status (4 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id_hash` | u32 | CRC-32 of the id bytes, as sent to processor A (0 for `bad_request`) |

On an error: every field (zero where not reached). Errors: `bad_request`, `link`, `storage`, `no_content`, `started`. Tool timeout: 75 s. **Destructive**: ask the user first. Build switch `XYF_USB_SET_DEFAULT`, not optional: the firmware does not build without it. Since 1.0.

### 0x41 `tfw.check`

Check that a firmware package on the device is official and that the device's own keys open it. Processor B reads the package header, verifies its P-224 signature with the public key in the device's one-time-programmable memory (OTP), then checks that the AES key there decrypts the package's name block and ZIP directory. It reads nothing else and changes nothing; the keys are read only for a well-formed header and nothing derived from them is sent. A cut (16-byte header: u32 `0x54434658`, package bytes, head bytes, tail offset; then the package's first head bytes and its bytes from the tail offset on) is checked as the package. ok: the check ran (see `verdict`); an error: the file could not be read.

| Request field (10 to 240 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `path` | cstr UTF-8, 10..240 B | absolute path under `/yaffs2/` of a `.tfw` file or a cut of one, NUL-terminated |

| Reply field, after the status (40 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `verdict` | u32 | 0 = pass; 1 = fail. The result |
| `reason` | u32 | 0 = pass; 1 = a read failed; 2 = not a package, or its sizes differ from the file; 3 = an AES key index other than 0; 4 = the device's one-time-programmable memory gave no key; 5 = the device's public key is not on the curve; 6 = the signature does not verify; 7 = the device's key does not decrypt the package; 8 = the decrypted ZIP directory is malformed. Why |
| `public_key_sha256` | bytes[32] | SHA-256 of the device's 56-byte public key; zero when none was read |

On an error: the status only. Errors: `bad_request`, `refused`, `link`, `storage`, `not_found`, `range`. Tool timeout: 60 s. Build switch `XYF_TFW_CHECK` (on in product builds; without it: `unsupported`). Since 1.2.

### 0x43 `library.boot`

Boot a library entry once, as PLAY on it in the library menu. After the ok reply the menu closes, USB goes away and the entry boots once; the default and the state files do not change. Errors boot nothing: an entry the menu does not list is `not_found`, one it lists without an `os.ldr` (not selectable there) `state`, one whose content is not installed `no_content` (make it the default to install its content), a lost link `link`.

| Request field (34 to 64 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | cstr ASCII, 2..32 B | library entry id: 1-31 of `a-z 0-9 _ -`, NUL-terminated |
| `sha256` | bytes[32] | confirmation: the SHA-256 of the id bytes, without the NUL |

Reply: the status only.

Errors: `bad_request`, `sha`, `link`, `not_found`, `state`, `no_content`. Tool timeout: 30 s. Since 1.7.

### 0x44 `mods.apply`

Start assembling mod firmware on the device (a job). Checks the request and that every input exists (`not_found`, `missing` says which), makes the output folder and answers at once; processor B then runs the job in small steps from its menu loop, which stays live (`job.status`, `job.cancel`). Reads only the generation's packages, the base entry, the stock catalog and the output; writes only the output folder: an entry's files as `<name>.part`, read back, renamed, `os.ldr` last. A failed or cancelled job leaves no `os.ldr`; it removes its files and folders (`debris` 1 in `job.status` when it could not). Before the job's first step B removes leftover `tmp/job-*` folders (bounded). A finished entry becomes library entry `mods-a` or `mods-b` (phase `finish`, detail `commit`): never the default or the boot-once entry; the absent one, else the one not written last; the old entry is renamed into `tmp/` first, then the new one into `firmware/`, then the old one removed. It is listed with its content not installed (`no_content`). A staged upload in progress is `busy`; no free job id, or both mods ids are the default and the boot-once entry, `state`.

| Request field (47 to 1460 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `base` | cstr ASCII, 2..32 B | library entry id whose `os.ldr` is the stock image; its `content.sha256` is the firmware's content list |
| `profile` | cstr ASCII, 2..32 B | `mods/<profile>/` (1-31 of `a-z 0-9 . _ -`, a letter or digit first) |
| `generation` | cstr ASCII, 2..32 B | `mods/<profile>/<generation>/`, the package set (as `profile`) |
| `machines` | cstr ASCII, 2..1024 B | 1 to 64 machine ids (library id form), comma-separated, in layout order |
| `extensions` | cstr ASCII, 1..256 B | 0 to 8 extension ids, comma-separated (empty: none) |
| `name` | cstr ASCII, 2..48 B | the entry's `info.txt` name: 1-47 printable bytes, no space at either end |
| `flags` | u32 | 0 = a known base only, standard memory; 1 = the user confirmed a base that is not a known one; 2 = the 4 MiB mod memory layout (since 1.12; the base's `expanded_module_base`); 3 = both. Bit 0: base trust; bit 1 (1.12): the 4 MiB layout, refused (`bad_request`) by a 1.11 device |
| `sha256` | bytes[32] | confirmation: the SHA-256 of every request byte before it |

| Reply field, after the status (8 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `job` | u32 | the job's id (0 when refused); its output folder is `/yaffs2/xy-forever/tmp/job-<id>/` |
| `missing` | u32 | 0 = none; 1 = the base's `os.ldr`; 2 = the base's `content.sha256`; 3 = `/yaffs2/content/op1_factory.json`; 4 = the generation's `base/info.txt`. With `not_found`: the input the device lacks |

On an error: every field (zero where not reached). Errors: `bad_request`, `sha`, `link`, `not_found`, `state`, `storage`. Tool timeout: 30 s. **Destructive**: ask the user first. Build switch `XYF_USB_FILE_WRITE`, not optional: the firmware does not build without it. Since 1.10.

### 0x45 `job.status`

Progress of the running or last job. A job id this boot has not started (none yet, for 0) is `not_found`.

| Request field (4 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `job` | u32 | the job's id; 0: the running or last job |

| Reply field, after the status (76 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `job` | u32 | its id |
| `phase` | u32 | 0 = idle; 1 = inputs; 2 = link; 3 = patch; 4 = content; 5 = write; 6 = verify; 7 = finish; 8 = done; 9 = failed; 10 = cancelled. 8, 9 and 10 are final |
| `done` | u32 | units of the phase done (inputs: bytes; link, patch: steps; content: packages; write, verify, finish: outputs) |
| `total` | u32 | of total (0: not known ahead) |
| `error` | u32 | 0 = none; 1 = argument; 2 = path; 3 = region; 4 = open; 5 = read; 6 = truncated; 7 = size; 8 = list; 9 = unlisted; 10 = sha256; 11 = info; 12 = base; 13 = linker; 14 = patch; 15 = content; 16 = write; 17 = rename; 18 = verify; 19 = cancelled; 20 = image; 21 = link. Why it failed (`native/mod_job.hpp`; 12 with code 18: a base that is not a known one, not confirmed; 17: also the library commit; 21: processor A did not answer) |
| `code` | u32 | the refusing step's own status number |
| `elapsed_ms` | u32 | since the start (to the end once final) |
| `steps` | u32 | steps run |
| `longest_ms` | u32 | the longest menu-loop pass the job took |
| `peak` | u32 | work-region bytes used at most |
| `debris` | u32 | 0 = nothing left behind; 1 = a failed job's files or folders may remain in its output folder. After a failed or cancelled job |
| `detail` | bytes[32] | ASCII, NUL-padded: which file, object, edit or check; when done, the library entry id (also for a content switch) |

On an error: the status only. Errors: `bad_request`, `not_found`. Tool timeout: 5 s. Build switch `XYF_USB_FILE_WRITE`, not optional: the firmware does not build without it. Since 1.10.

### 0x46 `job.cancel`

Stop the running job. Removes what the job wrote and answers once that is done; a job that already ended, or is in its library commit (phase `finish`, detail `commit`), or a content switch (`library.set_default`), is `state`.

| Request field (4 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `job` | u32 | the job's id; 0: the running job |

| Reply field, after the status (4 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `debris` | u32 | 0 = nothing left behind; 1 = files or folders may remain in its output folder. After the clean-up |

On an error: every field (zero where not reached). Errors: `bad_request`, `not_found`, `state`. Tool timeout: 60 s. Build switch `XYF_USB_FILE_WRITE`, not optional: the firmware does not build without it. Since 1.10.

## Events

### 0xd0 `log`

A progress line while `boot.install` or `boot.uninstall` runs.

Sent with seq 0 while an install writes the boot partition, as long as the tool keeps reading (the device stops sending after the first line that cannot be delivered). Lines like `xyf install step N value 0x...` mark the install's steps.

Payload (8 to 208 bytes):

| Field | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `zero` | u32 | always 0 |
| `ms` | u32 | device milliseconds since its service started |
| `text` | text ASCII, 0..200 B | ASCII, no NUL, at most `max_log_text` bytes |

## Examples

Whole frames in hex, as the device and the host tool encode them (checked by `tests/test_protocol_spec.py`). The spec file also holds byte streams (`streams`) with the frames a correct parser finds in each: noise before a frame; a bad CRC, then a good frame; a frame split at every byte; two frames back to back; an oversized length; a frame cut short, then a frame; frames split across reads; an event and a reply back to back; noise and a reply split across reads.

- Hello (`hello` request, seq 1): `58 46 01 01 00 00 00 00 4c 8d 06 32`
- Hello, answered (`hello` reply, seq 1, status `ok`); `info` = "XYF1;service=usb;role=b;proto=1.13;install=stock-88a06a7e;build=172;mode=product;payload=4160;read=1024;stage=7340032;cmds=000000010000007b001f000303ff00be;dev=1;stage2=0": `58 46 81 01 ae 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 58 59 46 31 3b 73 65 72 76 69 63 65 3d 75 73 62 3b 72 6f 6c 65 3d 62 3b 70 72 6f 74 6f 3d 31 2e 31 33 3b 69 6e 73 74 61 6c 6c 3d 73 74 6f 63 6b 2d 38 38 61 30 36 61 37 65 3b 62 75 69 6c 64 3d 31 37 32 3b 6d 6f 64 65 3d 70 72 6f 64 75 63 74 3b 70 61 79 6c 6f 61 64 3d 34 31 36 30 3b 72 65 61 64 3d 31 30 32 34 3b 73 74 61 67 65 3d 37 33 34 30 30 33 32 3b 63 6d 64 73 3d 30 30 30 30 30 30 30 31 30 30 30 30 30 30 37 62 30 30 31 66 30 30 30 33 30 33 66 66 30 30 62 65 3b 64 65 76 3d 31 3b 73 74 61 67 65 32 3d 30 0c a9 d0 72`
- Hello, answered by a pre-v1 device (build 153 and earlier) (`hello` reply, seq 1, status `ok`); `info` = "XYF1;service=usb;role=b;proto=1;install=stock-88a06a7e": `58 46 81 01 3a 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 58 59 46 31 3b 73 65 72 76 69 63 65 3d 75 73 62 3b 72 6f 6c 65 3d 62 3b 70 72 6f 74 6f 3d 31 3b 69 6e 73 74 61 6c 6c 3d 73 74 6f 63 6b 2d 38 38 61 30 36 61 37 65 26 35 15 c5`
- Read 1024 bytes from offset 0 (`file.read` request, seq 2); `path` = "/yaffs2/firmware.version", `offset` = 0, `length` = 1024: `58 46 03 02 21 00 00 00 2f 79 61 66 66 73 32 2f 66 69 72 6d 77 61 72 65 2e 76 65 72 73 69 6f 6e 00 00 00 00 00 00 04 00 00 68 98 97 a6`
- File.read, file not found (`file.read` reply, seq 2, status `not_found`): `58 46 83 02 04 00 00 00 08 00 00 00 a0 85 65 1d`
- Any request before hello is refused (`stage.begin` reply, seq 3, status `state`): `58 46 90 03 04 00 00 00 03 00 00 00 09 2c 86 11`
- Screen.read at offset 1024 (`screen.read` request, seq 4); `offset` = 1024: `58 46 04 04 04 00 00 00 00 04 00 00 61 6e 1b a8`
- Stage the 4 bytes `test` (`stage.begin` request, seq 5); `size` = 4, `crc32` = 3632233996, `sha256` = "9f86d081884c7d659a2feaa0c55ad015a3bf4f1b2b0b822cd15d6c15b0f00a08": `58 46 10 05 28 00 00 00 04 00 00 00 0c 7e 7f d8 9f 86 d0 81 88 4c 7d 65 9a 2f ea a0 c5 5a d0 15 a3 bf 4f 1b 2b 0b 82 2c d1 5d 6c 15 b0 f0 0a 08 e9 fa 8a c6`
- Stage.data, 4 bytes received (`stage.data` reply, seq 6, status `ok`); `received` = 4: `58 46 91 06 08 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 04 00 00 00 7d bf b5 ee`
- A write path outside the write area is refused (`file.write_staged` reply, seq 8, status `refused`); `written` = 0, `readback_crc` = 0: `58 46 93 08 0c 00 00 00 0e 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 84 89 a9 55`
- A common status comes alone, whatever on_error says (`file.write_staged` reply, seq 9, status `state`): `58 46 93 09 04 00 00 00 03 00 00 00 94 1d 9f 6f`
- Reboot into the menu (`device.reboot` request, seq 7); `target` = 2: `58 46 30 07 04 00 00 00 02 00 00 00 b1 10 8e 5d`
- An install log line (`log` event, seq 0); `zero` = 0, `ms` = 1234, `text` = "xyf install step 1 value 0x00001000": `58 46 d0 00 2b 00 00 00 00 00 00 00 d2 04 00 00 78 79 66 20 69 6e 73 74 61 6c 6c 20 73 74 65 70 20 31 20 76 61 6c 75 65 20 30 78 30 30 30 30 31 30 30 30 5c 41 97 15`

## Conformance suite

`protocol/v1.conformance.json` holds the conformance suite: the behaviour a v1 device must show, as data that any client can run. Each case is a named exchange: preconditions (`given`: a fresh boot before `hello`, files in the test area, simulator faults), requests by command name and field values (or raw bytes for malformed input and frame-level tests), and what must come back (status, field values, limits such as the device's `read=`), including reads that show what did not change. Every case says what it does (`effects`: none means read-only; `staging`, `writes_test_area`, `restarts`, `writes_device`, `boots_os`), what it needs (`needs`: simulator control, fixtures) and whether it is safe on a real device (`real_device`, else `why_not`). The keywords are documented in the file's `syntax` object.

A third-party client conforms when it runs every case with its own codec and transport: send the requests in order, one at a time, and check each expectation. Two runners exist: `python3 scripts/conformance.py --sim 127.0.0.1:7341` (or without `--sim` for the OP-XY, where only cases marked safe run and a guard refuses any request that could change more than the test area `/yaffs2/xy-forever/log/conformance/`), and `node clients/ts/test/conformance.ts --sim 127.0.0.1:7341` for the TypeScript module. Both read the same file; `--check` only interprets every case.

86 cases: 65 safe on a real device; 40 read-only, 37 use the staging, 21 write the test area, 6 restart the device, 5 change stored state outside it and 3 boot the OS (simulator only).

## Appendix: developer commands

Unstable: they may change or disappear in any version, outside the compatibility rules.

### 0x02 `diag.status`

Device counters as tagged binary blocks. Development aid: the USB service's counters, the processor link, the file server, boot timing and the last dry-run boot.

Request: empty (the device ignores any payload).

| Reply field, after the status (0 to 4092 bytes) | Type | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `blocks` | rest, 0..4092 B | a sequence of blocks `{u32 magic, u32 bytes, bytes...}`; the block layouts belong to the build (decoder: `xy_forever/census.py`) and change without notice |

On an error: the status only. Errors: none of its own. The reply never gains fields (it ends in `rest`). Tool timeout: 5 s. Since 1.0.

Types 0x05, 0x07, 0x33, 0x34, 0x42, 0x60 are internal test commands, described only in the spec file; tools must not send them.

## Reserved for later versions

Numbers decision 004 assigns for later items. Not answered by any build yet: nothing here exists on the wire. Types 0x60..0x7f: new developer commands (0x60 is a test command today). Types 0xd0..0xdf: events, seq 0 (0xD0 is log today; progress 0xD1 with item 4.3d).
